title: What the German skilled-worker rules mean for applicants from Pakistan
description: Germany is short of engineers, nurses, IT specialists and tradespeople. What the current skilled-worker rules offer applicants from Pakistan, and which parts of the process still take time.
html:
Germany needs more skilled workers than it trains, and the rules for coming from outside the EU have been loosened in several steps: the Opportunity Card for a job search without a contract, lower thresholds for the EU Blue Card and a wider list of recognised qualifications. For applicants from Pakistan this opens routes that did not exist a few years ago, in IT, engineering, healthcare and the skilled trades.

The practical bottlenecks are not the rules but the paperwork: the recognition of a Pakistani degree or diploma, the language level a given job requires, and appointment waiting times at the German missions in Islamabad and Karachi. Applicants who prepare the recognition documents early and book the appointment as soon as the checklist is complete are usually months ahead of those who wait for a job offer first.

The financial and insurance requirements of the visa do not change with the route: proof of funds where no employment contract exists, and health insurance from the day of arrival. Both can be arranged from Pakistan before the appointment, which is exactly what the {{product}} is for.
